title_en: Regulations on the Protection of Computer Software

articles.content_en: Article 1 These Regulations are formulated in accordance with the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China for the purpose of protecting the rights and interests of copyright owners of computer software, regulating the interests arising from the development, dissemination and use of computer software, encouraging the development and application of computer software, and promoting the development of the software industry and the informatization of the national economy.
Article 2 For the purposes of these Regulations, "computer software" (hereinafter referred to as "software") means computer programs and their related documentation.

Article 3 For the purposes of these Regulations, the following definitions shall apply:
(1) "Computer program" means a coded instruction sequence that can be executed by a computer or other device with information processing capability to achieve a certain result, or a symbolic instruction sequence or symbolic statement sequence that can be automatically converted into a coded instruction sequence. The source program and object program of the same computer program shall be deemed as one work.
(2) "Documentation" means written materials and diagrams, such as program design specifications, flow charts, and user manuals, used to describe the content, composition, design, functional specifications, development status, test results, and usage methods of the program.
(3) "Software developer" means a legal person or other organization that actually organizes the development, directly carries out the development, and bears responsibility for the developed software; or a natural person who independently completes the software development with his or her own conditions and bears responsibility for the software.
(4) "Software copyright owner" means a natural person, legal person, or other organization that enjoys copyright in the software in accordance with these Regulations.
Article 4 Software protected under these Regulations must be independently developed by the developer and fixed on some tangible medium.

Article 5 Chinese citizens, legal persons, or other organizations shall enjoy copyright in the software they develop, whether published or not, in accordance with these Regulations.
Software of foreigners or stateless persons that is first published within the territory of China shall enjoy copyright in accordance with these Regulations.
Copyright in software of foreigners or stateless persons, enjoyed in accordance with agreements concluded between the country of which the developer is a national or in which he or she has habitual residence and China, or in accordance with international treaties to which China is a party, shall be protected under these Regulations.

Article 6 The protection of software copyright under these Regulations shall not extend to the ideas, processing procedures, methods of operation, or mathematical concepts used in the development of the software.

Article 7 A software copyright owner may apply for registration with a software registration institution recognized by the copyright administration department under the State Council. The registration certificate issued by the software registration institution shall be prima facie evidence of the matters registered.
Fees shall be paid for software registration. The fee standards for software registration shall be prescribed by the copyright administration department under the State Council jointly with the competent pricing department under the State Council.

Article 9 The copyright in software shall belong to the software developer, unless otherwise provided in these Regulations.
In the absence of proof to the contrary, the natural person, legal person, or other organization whose name is affixed on the software shall be deemed to be the developer.

Article 10 The ownership of copyright in software developed jointly by two or more natural persons, legal persons, or other organizations shall be stipulated in a written contract signed by the joint developers. In the absence of a written contract or where the contract does not explicitly stipulate the ownership, if the jointly developed software can be used separately, each developer may independently enjoy copyright in the part developed by himself or herself; however, the exercise of such copyright shall not extend to the copyright in the jointly developed software as a whole. If the jointly developed software cannot be used separately, the copyright shall be jointly owned by all the joint developers and exercised by consensus; if consensus cannot be reached and there is no legitimate reason, none of the parties may prevent the other parties from exercising rights other than the right of transfer, provided that the proceeds arising therefrom shall be reasonably distributed among all the joint developers.

Article 11 The ownership of copyright in software developed under commission shall be stipulated in a written contract signed by the commissioning party and the commissioned party; in the absence of a written contract or where the contract does not explicitly stipulate the ownership, the copyright shall be owned by the commissioned party.

Article 12 The ownership and exercise of copyright in software developed under a task assigned by a state organ shall be stipulated in the project task document or contract; if the project task document or contract does not explicitly stipulate the ownership, the software copyright shall be owned by the legal person or other organization that undertook the task.

Article 14 Software copyright shall arise from the date on which the software development is completed.
The term of protection of software copyright of a natural person shall be the lifetime of the natural person and 50 years after his or her death, expiring on December 31 of the 50th year after the death of the natural person; where the software is jointly developed, it shall expire on December 31 of the 50th year after the death of the last surviving natural person.
The term of protection of software copyright of a legal person or other organization shall be 50 years, expiring on December 31 of the 50th year after the first publication of the software; however, if the software has not been published within 50 years from the date on which its development is completed, it shall no longer be protected under these Regulations.

Article 15 Where the software copyright belongs to a natural person, after the death of the natural person, within the term of protection of the software copyright, the successor of the software copyright may, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Succession Law of the People's Republic of China, inherit the rights provided for in Article 8 of these Regulations, other than the right of authorship.
Where the software copyright belongs to a legal person or other organization, after the change or termination of the legal person or other organization, the copyright shall, within the term of protection provided for in these Regulations, be owned by the legal person or other organization that succeeds to its rights and obligations; if there is no legal person or other organization that succeeds to its rights and obligations, the copyright shall be owned by the State.

Article 17 Where software is used by means of installation, display, transmission, or storage for the purpose of studying and researching the design ideas and principles embodied in the software, such use may be done without the permission of, and without payment of remuneration to, the software copyright owner.

Article 18 Where a software copyright owner licenses another person to exercise the software copyright, a license agreement shall be concluded.
Any right not explicitly licensed by the software copyright owner in the license agreement shall not be exercised by the licensee.

Article 19 Where a software copyright owner licenses another person to exclusively exercise the software copyright, the parties shall conclude a written contract.
If no written contract is concluded or the contract does not explicitly stipulate that the license is exclusive, the rights licensed to be exercised shall be deemed non-exclusive rights.
Article 20 Where a software copyright is transferred, the parties shall conclude a written contract.

Article 21 The parties that conclude a license contract for exclusive exercise of software copyright or a contract for transfer of software copyright may register with a software registration institution recognized by the copyright administration department under the State Council.

Article 22 Where a Chinese citizen, legal person, or other organization licenses or transfers software copyright to a foreigner, it shall comply with the relevant provisions of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Administration of Import and Export of Technologies.

Article 25 The amount of compensation for infringement of software copyright shall be determined in accordance with the provisions of Article 49 of the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China.

Article 26 Where a software copyright owner has evidence to prove that another person is committing or is about to commit an act infringing upon his or her rights, and that if such act is not stopped promptly, his or her lawful rights and interests will suffer irreparable harm, he or she may, in accordance with the provisions of Article 50 of the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China, apply to the People's Court for an order to stop the relevant act and for property preservation before instituting legal proceedings.

Article 27 For the purpose of stopping an infringing act, if the evidence may be lost or becomes difficult to obtain later, the software copyright owner may, in accordance with the provisions of Article 51 of the Copyright Law of the People's Republic of China, apply to the People's Court for evidence preservation before instituting legal proceedings.

Article 28 If the publisher or producer of a software copy cannot prove that its publication or production is legally authorized, or if the distributor or lessor of a software copy cannot prove that the copy distributed or leased has a lawful source, they shall bear legal liability.

Article 29 Where software developed by a software developer is similar to an existing software due to the limited availability of expression forms, it shall not constitute an infringement of the copyright of the existing software.

Article 30 Where the holder of a software copy does not know and has no reasonable ground to know that such copy is an infringing copy, he or she shall not bear liability for compensation; however, he or she shall cease using and destroy such infringing copy. If ceasing the use and destroying the infringing copy would cause significant losses to the user of the copy, the user may continue to use it after paying a reasonable fee to the software copyright owner.

Article 31 Disputes over infringement of software copyright may be mediated.
Disputes over software copyright contracts may be submitted to an arbitration institution for arbitration in accordance with the arbitration clause in the contract or a written arbitration agreement reached afterwards.
If the parties have not included an arbitration clause in the contract and have not reached a written arbitration agreement afterwards, they may directly institute legal proceedings with the People's Court.

Article 32 Infringing acts committed before the coming into force of these Regulations shall be dealt with in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State in effect at the time when the infringing acts were committed.

Article 33 These Regulations shall come into force as of January 1, 2002. The Regulations on the Protection of Computer Software promulgated by the State Council on June 4, 1991 shall be abolished simultaneously.
